tip: 'drwy' (through) triggers soft mutation: 'cerddoriaeth' becomes 'gerddoriaeth' in 'drwy gerddoriaeth'.
'heb' plus a verb means not having done it: 'heb ffonio' here is hadn't called, the negative of 'wedi ffonio'.
Unreal conditions pair 'pe bawn i' (if I were) with 'byddwn i' (I would). Both take the same '-wn' ending.
For a negative condition, add 'na' after 'pe': 'pe na bawn i wedi colli' means if I hadn't missed.
An adjective after the linking 'yn' soft mutates: 'trist' becomes 'drist' in 'yn drist' (sad).
'yn' (in) triggers nasal mutation and itself becomes 'yng': 'canol' turns into 'yng nghanol' (in the middle of).
'gyda' (with) triggers aspirate mutation: 'tro' becomes 'thro' in 'gyda thro annisgwyl' (with a twist).
After a form of 'gallu' (can), the following verb soft mutates: 'gwahanu' becomes 'wahanu' in 'allwch wahanu'.
To report that it was, Welsh uses 'fod', from 'bod': 'credwn i fod e'n wir' = I believed it was true.
'trwy' before a verb means by doing it: 'trwy weithio' = by working.
Welsh wraps your around the noun: 'dy gar di' = your car, 'dy' before and 'di' after 'gar'.
The ending '-wyd' makes a past passive with no named doer: 'anfonwyd y neges' = the message was sent.
Adjectives after a feminine noun soft-mutate: after 'het', 'tal' and 'du' become 'dal' and 'ddu' in 'het dal ddu' = tall black hat.
'byddwn i' means I would while 'bydda i' means I will: 'byddwn i'n hoffi' = I would like.
Welsh has no verb to have. Possession uses 'mae' with 'gen i', literally is with me: 'mae gen i lawer' = I have lots.
A Welsh verb doubles as an -ing noun: 'dysgu' means both to learn and learning, as in 'mae dysgu' = learning is.
A verb's object soft-mutates: 'digwyddiad' becomes 'ddigwyddiad' after 'trefnodd' = the students organised an event.
Welsh passives use 'cael' plus 'ei' plus a verb: 'cael ei gerfio' = gets carved, 'cerfio' softening to 'gerfio' after 'ei'.
'yn' meaning in nasal-mutates the next word and becomes 'yng': 'cefn' turns into 'yng nghefn' = in the back of.
'erioed' means never only about the past: 'dw i erioed wedi bod' = I have never been. For future never, use 'byth'.
For a real if, use 'os' with the future 'bydd': 'os bydd hi'n bwrw glaw' = if it rains. Keep 'pe' for unreal ifs.
Front a phrase for emphasis, then put 'y' before the verb: 'yn yr eisteddfod y clywais i' = it was there that I heard.
Regret about the past pairs 'pe bawn i wedi' with 'byddwn i wedi': 'pe bawn i wedi astudio' = if I had studied harder.
'sut wyt ti' uses 'ti', the familiar you for friends and family: it means how are you.
